title: Eighteen Pages and One Long Silence
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：dialogue　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dialogue 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the writer ① wrote a dialogue that no editor in the town would have printed, and he said the writing was the whole of the chapter. The ② dialogue, meaning the talk and not the discussion, ran eighteen pages and stayed unspoken on the page; a dialogue, he said, is the only thing in a chapter that is judged by how long it is left unread.

Every ③ dialogue in that chapter had the same long silence in the middle of it, and the ④ dialogue at the end, meaning the one they kept for the last scene and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever rehearsed twice. A dialogue, his reader said, is nine parts listening and one part somebody willing to speak; the writer said the listening is the part that fills eighteen pages.

The mediator meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the dialogue was the whole of the meeting, meaning the discussion and not the talk. The ⑥ dialogue, meaning the discussion and not any of that, is the only thing in a meeting that everybody attends and nobody concludes; dialogue, she said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a talk and a discussion. She said the discussion is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ dialogue had become a line in a script, and the script had become an argument about the long silence. The ⑧ dialogue of the whole thing, the writer wrote in March, was one chapter and eighteen pages of listening; dialogue, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to listen. She said the listening was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dialogue I remember is the one at the end, which was performed in 1976 and is still described as the strangest in the chapter. A ⑩ dialogue, the reader said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being spoken; every dialogue, she said, is a discussion that has agreed to look like a talk. She said the discussion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 对话；对白（指那一章里写出的那一段）
B. n. 对白（指那些交谈本身，与那场商谈相对）
C. 固定搭配：write a dialogue 写一段对话
D. n. 对白（指留给最后一幕用的那一段）
E. n. 对话；对白（抽象总称，指一整章的对白写作）
F. n. 对白（指脚本里写到、被排定的那一段）
G. n. 对话；商谈（指会议上进行的那场沟通）
H. n. 商谈（抽象总称，指人人出席却无人收束的那场）

items.q: wrote a dialogue that no editor in the town would have printed
The dialogue, meaning the talk and not the discussion
the dialogue was the whole of the meeting
the dialogue had become a line in a script
The dialogue of the whole thing
A dialogue, the reader said in 1978

answers.why: write a dialogue 意为“写一段对话”，1954 年作家写了一段全城没有一位编辑肯刊印的对话。
dialogue 意为“对白”，指那些交谈本身而不是那场商谈，它写了十八页而从未被念出。
dialogue 意为“对话”，指那一章里每一段对话，每一段中间都有同一段长长的沉默。
dialogue 意为“对白”，指留给最后一幕用的那一段，是唯一有人排练过两次的。
dialogue 意为“对话、商谈”，指会议上进行的那场沟通，调解人说这场商谈就是那次会议的全部。
dialogue 意为“商谈”，指人人出席却无人收束的那场而不是那些交谈本身，是会议里人人都出席、却无人收束的东西。
dialogue 意为“对白”，指脚本里写到、被排定的那一段，到 1962 年这段对白成了脚本里的一行。
dialogue 意为“对话、对白”，作家三月写道，整件事的对白是一章和十八页的倾听。
dialogue 意为“对话”，我记得的是末尾那一段，1976 年被演出，至今仍被说成那一章里最奇的一段。
dialogue 为抽象总称，读者 1978 年说，一段对话是唯一会因为被念出来而变得更好的东西。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。

那段对白，指的是那些交谈本身而不是那场商谈，写了十八页而从未被念出。（dialogue）

调解人说这场商谈就是那次会议的全部，指的是那场沟通而不是那些交谈。（dialogue）
